'''Numerical error''' is the error that arises in [[Numerical analysis|numerical computations]] due to limitations in representing real numbers and performing arithmetic operation on computers. These errors commonly appear in [[software engineering]] and [[mathematics]]. 
[[File:Time series of the Tent map for the parameter m=2.0 which shows numerical error.svg|thumb|right|Time series of the [[Tent map]] for the parameter m=2.0 which shows numerical error: "the plot of time series (plot of x variable with respect to number of iterations) stops fluctuating and no values are observed after n=50". Parameter m= 2.0, initial point is random.]]
==Types==
Numerical error in [[Computation|computations]] generally arises from several sources. The most common sources are [[round-off error]] and [[truncation error]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Burden |first=Richard |title=Numerical Analysis |last2=Faires |first2=Douglas |date=August 9, 2010 |publisher=[[Cengage Group|Cengage Learning]] |isbn=978-0538733519 |edition=9th}}</ref>

It can be the combined effect of two kinds of error in a calculation. The first is referred to as [[round-off error]] and is caused by the finite [[Precision (computer science)|precision]] of computations involving [[floating-point]] numbers.
The second, usually called [[truncation error]], is the difference between the exact mathematical solution and the approximate solution obtained when simplifications are made to the mathematical equations to make them more amenable to calculation.

==Measure==
Floating-point numerical error is often measured in ULP ([[unit in the last place]]), which represents the distance between two adjacent [[Floating-point arithmetic|floating-point]] numbers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Units in the last pace (ULP) |url=https://learn.arm.com/learning-paths/servers-and-cloud-computing/multi-accuracy-libamath/ulp/ |access-date=March 11, 2026 |website=Arm Learning Paths}}</ref>
